requirements.text: be one command-line program whose command line is its only interface: no library for callers, no socket, and every invocation ends by itself when its operation is done
run no resident process of any kind: no daemon, no watcher, no launch agent, no timer

work with nothing of Arbol installed or running, and contain no built-in product-specific name, path, variable or message except the explicit packaged data of MYC-D37; repository names and shared document selections supplied in settings are data

keep mutable knowledge and operation state only in its own PostgreSQL index database with ParadeDB, at the address supplied by the settings; keep only the distribution files of MYC-15 outside it, and read `~/.mycel/config.toml` at the start of every invocation
never write its settings file
follow the command-line rules above for the repository, output, errors and exit status
report every failure as one error object with a code from the closed list, and never ask a caller to match error text

change the structure of the index store only in `mycel init`, and refuse every other store-dependent command with `store_format` when the store's format is not the one its Build knows; diagnostic `info` and grep without its Mycel tail remain available
be built into numbered Builds as MYC-15 says and report the build number of the Build that runs in `info`

call model services only for embedding, explicit classify or live drift evaluation, and the configured summary-writing operation; make no Jev/reviewer calls from ingest/search/read/reporting or dry-runs, forward no Mycel credentials to child programs, and run no git command that changes a repository
have an automated check for every requirement of MYC-1 to MYC-16 before that requirement counts as implemented, the store-backed ones against a store made for the test and discarded after it
keep the guides of this corpus true to the program: a change to a command, an option or a reply changes the guide that describes it in the same change
take the repositories, their folders and whether each is enabled from the settings file alone, and keep no second copy that a command consults

refuse commands that need valid settings when the file cannot be read, a table or key is unknown, or a known key has the wrong type; name the file and fault, and give detailed unknown-key diagnostics as MYC-5.3 specifies
derive the folders of an organization's member from the organization, and let folders given for the repository itself win

act on the repository a command names, or on the one whose configured folder contains the current directory, the longest folder winning, and refuse the command when neither gives one. An organization's name, or a directory in an organization's folder but in none of its members, gives every enabled member of that organization

use repository names as written in the settings; no repository, folder or alias is built in, apart from the explicit packaged shared selections and scan exclusion of MYC-D37, which create no repository, alias or folder fallback
read the document corpus and the code corpus with one scan that skips the same folders in both, skips what the repository's `.gitignore` excludes, and takes the file types the settings list
skip a file whose content is unchanged since the last pass, and notice every changed file whatever other step ran before
refuse a pass that would find none of a corpus's documents on disk while the store holds some that were there, unless the caller confirms it

split a Markdown file at its headings, each heading owning the text down to the next heading of any level, with text before the first heading as a chunk of its own and no heading recognised inside a code fence
name a section by its heading path and keep that name unique within the file
hash a section's body without its heading, after Unicode normalisation and with white space collapsed, and hash its title separately
read the frontmatter of a document as settings and keep it out of the chunks' text
split a code file along its structure: functions, classes as a header plus one chunk per method, and the other top-level declarations of its language, each with language, kind and line span
keep a decorator and a leading comment in the chunk of the symbol they belong to
name every chunk of a code file uniquely within the file, and so that adding or removing one chunk changes no other chunk's name
keep a file that cannot be parsed as one whole-file chunk
recognise a chunk again in two rounds over its file: by name first, then by content among what is left. A chunk with no body is never matched by content
recognise chunks of code and of documents by the same rules, a renamed function included
keep a document's and its chunks' identity when the file is moved without a change
record every decision about identity (unchanged, edited, renamed, new, removed) with the pass that made it, and show them on request

delete the rows of a version that is found in no location, and of a chunk that has no version left, in the pass that finds it so, and only when that pass read every location of the repository. Keep no removed chunk row for a time or marked as gone; retain missing-source evidence only in surviving dependants as MYC-2.24 specifies
apply each file in one transaction: its hash, its chunks and its identity decisions together or not at all

reconcile files only in the repositories an invocation names, or all enabled ones when it says so; permit dependency records, stale marks, retries of valid refs targeting those repositories and their activity entries in affected dependants under their repository locks, and change no unrelated rows
never run a command that changes a checkout or fetches from a remote, and read the files of a repository as they are: the disk as it lies, branches and stashes from the git store
let one pass at a time work on a repository, and tell a second caller plainly that it did nothing because another pass is running
report per repository the documents and chunks that are on disk, those found only in a branch or a stash, and when the last pass ran
remove every row of a repository on request, and nothing of any other repository
write nothing in a command that only reports

refuse a command that needs the folders of a repository whose name is found under several organizations and that gives no code folder, naming the organizations, and let commands for other repositories go on
read, besides the files on disk, the files of every local branch and of every stash of the checkout a folder lies in, by the rules of the scan, and read no branch of a remote
store one version of a chunk for each text it has, record for every version the locations it is found in, and give a chunk one identifier in all of them

include Markdown under both `artifact_root` and `code_root` in the document corpus, independently of source-code `code_subdirs`, applying the common skip list and `.gitignore`; split it at headings and keep document origin in search and read replies

retain a document's actual root and path for identity, Source Refs and reads; index a file reached through overlapping roots once per disk, branch or stash location, distinguish different files sharing a relative path, report ambiguous addresses and silently merge none; preserve existing unambiguous source identities and the identity rules for genuine moves

retain exact text versions separately from normalized comparison hashes under MYC-16; keep identity through recognized renames/moves, reuse a version only for identical stored text, preserve inherited pins for normalized-equivalent/renamed text and retain deleted-source evidence solely in surviving dependant-owned blobs
read `role`, `status: heartwood` with `implemented` and `outdated`, `generated` and `sources` from a document's frontmatter as YAML, and ignore every other key
report a frontmatter block it cannot read and a known key with a value it does not take, for the file they are in
read the Source Refs of a section from the sources comment in its text, one per line, and attach the frontmatter's `sources` to the document's first chunk
ignore a sources comment inside a code fence or inline code

resolve refs only into registered, enabled repositories: a path to one physical file under its actual code or artifact root, a symbol to that file's code chunk and class family, and a heading to that file's document section by full path or unique bare title; deduplicate overlapping-root aliases and never resolve a colliding file path without an explicit root

retain and report malformed refs, unregistered/disabled targets, valid refs finding nothing, colliding file paths and ambiguous headings in the pass reply and list on request; include root-aware candidates for ambiguous paths and silently drop none

treat a ref into an unregistered or disabled repository as invalid, create no edge from it, deactivate a previously resolved declared edge when its target becomes ineligible, and retain the ref and its fault for reporting. Check eligibility on every pass; no outside-reference exemption applies
retain a valid unresolved ref and try it again on every pass of its repository and of the enabled repository it points into; recheck invalid refs when the settings change
hold for each resolved ref into an enabled repository an edge from the source to the chunk, storing the source's content hash, and remove the edge when the ref leaves the file
hold an asserted edge apart from a declared one between the same two ends, so that neither a file nor a command removes the other's
refuse an edge from a chunk to itself and an edge that would close a circle, and report it

work out a chunk's role on every pass: `derived` with at least one edge pointing at it or a retained dependency whose previously resolved source is missing from an enabled repository; otherwise what its file declares; otherwise `authored` for code and `unclassified` for a section
mark a chunk stale when a source of it has a content hash other than the one its edge stores, with a reason that names the source by repository, path and name
mark a chunk stale when a source of it is gone, with a reason that says so

pass staleness on through every downstream dependency across repositories, keeping every applicable reason, direct ones before passed-on ones; an indirect reason names the original source and the path through intermediate chunks
never mark a Heartwood or generated chunk stale, and pass nothing on through it
decide staleness by comparing hashes, with no model and no network

run detection after both corpora of each checked repository were ingested, propagate changed stale state through all downstream dependants across repositories under their locks, and change no unrelated dependency records or marks; report updates that could not be applied as pending
write a new hash into an edge only when the edge is made, when the chunk that rests on it is itself edited, or when its owner confirms the chunk. A change elsewhere in the chunk's file writes none
list on request the stale chunks of a repository, each with its reasons and the sources behind them, alongside the stored Drifts and exact-evidence lifecycle specified by MYC-14/MYC-16
state in the status of a repository how many of its chunks are stale, how many of its refs are valid but unresolved and how many are invalid because their repository is unregistered or disabled

work out edges and staleness for the versions of chunks that are on disk, treat a source that is not on disk as gone, and keep the hash an edge stores for each version of the chunk that rests on it, so that a switch of branch renews none

implement all five designs required by MYC-D13: stored Drifts, judging changed dependencies through selected Jev classification without a change-size threshold and its debounce/review policy under MYC-D28, relations without authority, recorded verification and generated edges. Follow their accepted MYC-7/MYC-14/MYC-16 contracts; defer none merely for task volume

retain in a surviving dependant the natural place, kind and pinned hash of a previously resolved source that is removed, report it as `source_removed`, and retry its resolution without renewing that baseline; retain no deleted source chunk or version for this purpose
use MYC-16's portable qualified addresses and central typed resolver, including file bytes and pinned class-family membership, and return canonical addresses in places and ambiguity candidates

capture exact dependant-owned baseline manifests atomically with authorized pins, preserve per-version/inherited baselines across branches, renames and normalized-equivalent edits, and expose missing/corrupt evidence without substituting a new baseline

list with `mycel undocumented` the code chunks of a repository's on-disk versions that no document section describes by a direct declared or asserted dependency in either direction, optionally only below given paths, sorted by root, path and name
embed the complete text of every version of every chunk of an enabled repository, in whatever location it is found, with one named model, and store the model's name with every part's vector
start every part's input with the plan's place line: path, symbol and kind for code; path and heading path for a document. The chunk's stored text stays as it is in the file
embed a query as typed, with the model's query input type; check its complete input locally and refuse it without truncation when it exceeds the model's limit

treat a part as pending exactly when its repository is enabled and it has no vector of the current model and no recorded failure, and allow other pending parts of a version to proceed when one part fails

keep a plan and one vector per part for each exact-text chunk version, model and dimensions: any change to stored text, including a heading or symbol rename, is a new version without vectors; keep the saved plan, place line and vectors through metadata-only name, place or location changes when exact stored text is unchanged
embed only the repositories an invocation names, or all enabled ones when it says so. No other command embeds chunks of a repository it was not asked about
store completed parts' vectors batch by batch, retain them after interruption or failure, and send only missing or explicitly retried failed parts on the next pass
try a request again, with growing pauses, when it failed for a reason that can pass, and give up on the pass only after the attempts its settings allow
find the parts at fault when the service rejects a batch for its content, record each failure and reason on its part, and embed the other pending parts
report without sending anything the chunk versions and input parts an embed would send, roughly how many tokens including repeated place lines, and any planning failures
report per repository version counts for embedded, pending and failed under the coverage rules, and separate part counts; pending parts are exactly what an ordinary next embed would send
never send text of a disabled, unknown or removed repository to the embedding service

read the key from the place its settings name and nowhere else; document one Keychain identity that Arbol or another compatible editor can create and replace and that Mycel can read, without duplicate secrets or an Arbol dependency; never print the key, pass it as an argument or write it to a file
create a new plan with pending parts when the model changes, without carrying failures from the old model into it, and never search vectors with a query embedded by another model

split each chunk version's text into ordered parts whose concatenation is exactly the complete stored text, with offsets at Unicode character boundaries; embed every part independently without trimming, summarising or changing the logical chunk's identity
retain each part's range, order, saved input context, vector and failure under its chunk version and model, and mark that version fully embedded only when every part of a valid plan has a vector

measure every complete input and batch against the selected model and provider limits before sending, disable provider truncation, and record a local failure without discarding text when a valid input plan cannot be made

package and verify each supported model's official pinned tokenizer and catalog; count with that tokenizer locally without padding, truncation, approximate counts or runtime downloads, and retain tokenizer, planner and limit provenance in every saved plan

produce deterministic version-1 part ranges and batches under the algorithm above, using original UTF-8 offsets and remeasuring each final complete input, with full coverage or an explicit planning failure

send explicit model, dimensions, float output, input type and disabled truncation; follow the request deadline, transient retry and authentication/model failure rules above without replacing saved inputs

validate every returned vector's index, finite values and dimensions, atomically persist a wholly validated batch for still-retained versions, discard vectors only for versions deleted meanwhile, and report sanitized stopping reasons without exposing provider bodies or credentials

search the repository an invocation names, or the one the current directory belongs to, and refuse the search when neither gives one. An organization's name or folder gives its enabled members (MYC-1.4, MYC-4.24). No repository's name is built in
leave a disabled repository out of every search

add to a search that includes documents only the document files selected by `search.shared_documents`, whose entries name an enabled repository and files or recursive folders relative to its `artifact_root`. Default to all Mycel artifact files and only Arbol's `GLOSSARY.md`; add none to a code-only search
match by meaning on fully embedded chunk versions and by exact wording on the complete text of every chunk, including versions with partial or failed embedding coverage
match by wording on a chunk's text, its name and its path
take the identifier route for a query made only of letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `#`, `/` and `-`, including one plain word, and the question route for any other
on the identifier route, score by reciprocal rank fusion of the two arms with equal weight
on the question route, score by cosine similarity and place wording hits the meaning arm missed below every scored result
on the question route, follow the closest document sections of the searched repository one step along their Source Refs to the code they cite, and name the section on every result it delivered
raise the score of a chunk found both directly and through a section once, however many sections cite it
apply the down-weights for tests, generated code and structural chunks to a chunk however it entered the ranking, and lift the first two when the query asks for them
take the patterns that recognise tests and generated code from the repository's settings, with version 1's as defaults
return a document among code results only when it clearly beats the best direct code match, at most twice per search, and never a routing file. The rule holds on both routes and for both arms

give every result and its citations the same dependency annotations: stale and Heartwood marks, every stale reason naming its original source and intermediate path, and whether checking the explicit dependencies completed, with ref faults; never present an unchecked chunk as verified current
name in the reply the route taken and whether the meaning arm took part, with the reason when it did not
answer by wording alone, and say so, when the query cannot be embedded. A search does not fail for that reason
order equal scores and the entries of `documented_in` by a stated rule, so that the same index and query give the same reply

before every kind of search check and ingest changes in the enabled repositories supplying its results or selected shared documents and recursively in their explicit declared or asserted upstream sources, including valid unresolved refs; resolve dependencies and propagate affected stale marks without broadening result scope. The caller can turn the entire check off

share one existing time limit across the check, recursive source checks, ingest and propagation; search the index as it is when work cannot finish, report each required repository's completion or pending state and reason, and mark the affected result dependency checks incomplete
state in the reply how many on-disk chunk versions lack complete current-model embedding coverage, including partial coverage, failed parts and failed plans

write during a search only the reconciled files, dependency records, affected stale marks and reasons, and activity entries required by its check and ingest of changes; change no unrelated rows and neither generate dependant text nor embed pending chunks
refuse a number of results below 1 or above 100, and an empty query, in every kind of search

identify each file-backed result by its actual configured root and relative path, giving a readable absolute file only when it exists within that root; keep checkout Markdown as document origin, distinguish colliding relative paths and otherwise explain why the file cannot be read
search the enabled members of an organization one by one and return one reply per member, with the requested result limit per member, never one merged list
keep an evaluation set of queries with the chunks each should find, report recall at 3 and at 10 for it, and change a ranking rule or a constant only with that report for before and after
answer from the versions of chunks that are on disk, and never return a version that is found only in a branch or a stash

score a fully embedded chunk by its best matching part, collapse part matches before all candidate, bridge and result limits and ranks, and return each logical chunk once without accumulating score raises from its parts
return MYC-16 canonical qualified addresses on results and citations, distinguishing actual root bindings from origin and index-only namespaces while preserving stable chunk identifiers
say in each code result whether any document section describes it by a direct declared or asserted dependency in either direction, independently of embeddings and of the query
read its settings from `~/.mycel/config.toml`, or from the file `MYCEL_CONFIG` names, and from nowhere else
know exactly the keys of the table above, use the default of a key that is absent, and check every value for its type and range

refuse unknown tables and keys with `settings` before index access or service calls; identify the file, every unknown fully qualified key and its line when available, explain the fault and accepted keys or an unambiguous correction, and never echo supplied values; `info` reports these faults and `grep` only omits its Mycel tail

refuse every command except `info` and `mycel grep` with `settings` when the file is missing, is not valid TOML, holds an unknown table or key, or holds a known key with a wrong value, naming the file and the key or line
run `mycel info` whatever the state of the settings, and show every fault there
take `~` at the start of a folder as the home folder, and refuse a folder that is not an absolute path after that
read no environment variable of its own other than `MYCEL_CONFIG` and `MYCEL_GREP_PLAIN`

refuse with `settings` a store address that carries a password; take the key of the embedding service from the command the settings name or else from its Keychain item, and the password of the store from its Keychain item
start a command that gives a secret without a shell, take its output without the final line break as the secret, and treat a status other than 0 as no secret
read a Keychain item with the system's `security` program, under the service and account named above
never write a secret to standard output, standard error, the store, a file outside its named encrypted Keychain item, or the environment of a program it starts
list in `mycel repos` every repository of the file with the folders worked out for it, where each folder comes from, and its fault when it has one
validate supported model/dimension pairs, finite classifier limits and complete reviewer command/provider/model/revision configuration before index or network access

read Jev's key only for explicit classification or live drift qualification from the named Keychain item, forward none of Mycel's credentials to reviewer commands, and acquire no Jev or Voyage credential during dry-run

validate the complete reviewer command/provider/model/revision configuration and exact argv/revision syntax, resolve only the first-member leading tilde, and document the protocol-1 setup without storing credentials or running a dry-run probe

provide `mycel api-key voyage` and `mycel api-key jev` to read a nonempty printable-ASCII key from a terminal without echo, refuse absent or unsafe terminal input with `invalid_input`, create or replace its named login-Keychain item through `/usr/bin/security` with that program explicitly trusted for reading, keep the key out of argv, output, logs, plaintext files and child environments, and return only the provider, item identity and replacement flag

keep mutable knowledge and invocation state between runs in one index store, with distribution/build files owned separately by MYC-15, and keep in it no copy of the settings, no secret and nothing of another product
take the store's address from the setting `store.address` alone, with no address built in and no variable that overrides it
refuse a command with `store_unavailable` when the store cannot be reached, say so in `mycel info` without refusing it, and run grep in `mycel grep` without the store
hand the store's address and password to no program it starts
make the structure, both search indexes included, only in `mycel init`, and write no repository and no default row there
write a format number into the store, and bring an older format forward in `mycel init`, one format at a time, each step in one transaction

refuse `mycel init` with `store_format` on a store with a newer format, and with `refused` on a database that holds tables that are not Mycel's or when a needed extension is missing, naming the reason

hold the number of dimensions of a vector as part of the structure; when the settings name another number, change it only in `mycel init`, removing the vectors of the old size, and until then refuse `embed` with `store_format` and answer a search by wording alone
write each change of the table above in one transaction, and let a command that only reads see one state of the store
let one pass and one embed at a time work on a repository, and passes on different repositories run side by side
never wait for another invocation: say at once that the work was not done and why
hold every lock in the store through the connection of the invocation that took it, so that it ends with the process

refuse with `busy` a `repos remove` for a repository on which a pass, embed, classification, summary operation or pinning/evidence mutation is at work, and every command except `info` and `grep` while `mycel init` changes the structure
give each repository its own entry in the reply of a command over one or several, end with status 1 when any was not done as asked, and write the full reply in that case too
leave rows whose repository the settings do not name, or name as switched off, out of every search, embed and pass, and delete them only on `repos remove`
list in `mycel status --all` every repository name that has rows in the store, and say for each whether the settings know it
read and write no table of version 1
retain only MYC-16 owning-reference-protected evidence outside searchable located versions, capture/repin it atomically, and collect only unreferenced owner-repository blobs

create a unique index-generation UUID when initializing an empty store, preserve it through ordinary ingest and migrations, and report it in init/info/activity so a lost-store rebuild cannot impersonate old evidence
implement nonblocking classification, summary, pinning and evidence-lease/removal locks with distinct advisory namespaces and exact invocation liveness; hold no pass lock during model calls
read the relations of a section from a `related` comment in its text, one ref per line, with the forms, the rules and the fault reports of Source Refs
hold a relation that was asserted with `mycel relate` apart from one a file declares, so that neither removes the other
mark a chunk stale with `related_changed` when a chunk it is related to no longer has the stored hash, and clear the mark by the rule of MYC-2.19
pass nothing on from a relation, give no role by it, refuse no circle of relations, and leave relations out of the search's bridge and of `documentedIn`
record with every `mycel confirm` the hash of the chunk's text, the hash of every source and related chunk, who vouches, whether by `read` or by `check`, and when
treat a chunk as verified exactly while its newest record matches its text and the text of everything it was checked against, and keep records that no longer apply as history
confirm a chunk that has no source, and list the verifications of a repository on request
hold a generated edge apart from a declared and an asserted one between the same two ends, and accept none from a file or from a command
pin a generated edge only when its text is produced, and refuse `mycel confirm` for generated text with `refused`
mark generated text stale by the rules of detection and pass staleness on through it

keep an edge or a relation whose source was deleted, with the source's place and the pinned hash; mark the dependant with `source_removed`; join the edge to a chunk that appears at that place again; and drop it when the dependant is edited or confirmed or the link is taken away
delete the matching asserted source selection and dependant on `--remove`, and nothing a file declares
resolve relations through MYC-16, pin all selected members and membership atomically, preserve assertion baselines on an identical no-op, and renew them only by edit or confirmation
confirm one exact current on-disk dependant version atomically with its pins and verification; refuse changed-since-ingest inputs and new invalid references without mutation
determine verification applicability from the exact dependant version, source text and selection membership, and retain record-owned evidence for the verification history
publish generated pins only with successfully generated text, retain the exact request evidence, and expose stale generated text as regeneration work without semantic classification
return the relation assertion/removal result and complete verification evidence; make verification listing read-only, deterministically ordered and successful when empty

summarise the sections of one repository's documents that are on disk and fully embedded, leaving out Heartwood documents, documents declared `generated`, code, sections of the code overview and summaries
count in its reply the sections left out because they are not embedded
group by the vectors with version 1's method and starting values, give the same groups for the same vectors, and place a section embedded in several parts by the mean of its parts' vectors

build in levels up to five, stop when ten or fewer nodes are left at the top, summaries and members moved up counted together, or when a level produced no summary, and move a group of one up a level without a summary
write no summary text itself: start the command `summaries.command` once for each summary, without a shell, in an empty folder, with the whole request on standard input
take a status other than 0, an empty answer and no answer within five minutes as a failure, try a failed summary once more, and record the reason of one that failed again
run at most `summaries.at_once` requests at the same time
refuse actual `build` and `regenerate` with `settings` when the settings name no command, and keep dry-runs, status, removal and search working
make each request of an instruction, a task and the group's sections, each section with its place line and its complete text, in the order of path and position
divide a group whose request would pass 48,000 characters until every part fits, and write a summary for each part, so that no section of a group is left out
give a single section that is longer than a whole request a request to itself, cut to the limit, and name it in the reply

take the instruction and the task from the folder `summaries.instructions` when the settings name one, and otherwise from the texts built into the program, putting the sections in the place of the mark `$sections` in the task
store a summary as a chunk with the origin `summary`, its level, the whole text the command printed, and a generated edge from every section it was written from
embed summaries by the rules of MYC-3, and in a build embed each level before grouping the next
put a new set of summaries in the old one's place in one transaction, only when every level is complete, and otherwise leave the old set untouched
report with `--dry-run` the levels, groups and number of requests of a build, or the summaries a `regenerate` would write, starting no command and writing nothing
write again, on `regenerate`, only the stale summaries, lowest level first, each in its place with the members that still exist, and pin its edges
delete a summary that has no member left, and leave stale a summary whose request failed
never write or rewrite a summary in a pass, a search or any command other than `summaries build` and `summaries regenerate`
report for a repository the summaries of each level, how many are stale, how many sections are in a summary, in none, and not embedded, and whether a command is set
remove every summary of a repository and its edges on request

let summaries of the searched repository compete in a search as documents do, leave them out of a search for code only, never follow one to code, and return one with the origin `summary` and without a file
report a ref to a summary in a file as a fault, and refuse with `invalid_input` a `derive` or `relate` that names one
use and record the deterministic `mycel-summary-v1` grouping profile and report invalid numerical inputs or failed fitting
validate configured command and prompt files before requests; retain the exact generation request, response and member evidence under MYC-16
keep staged summaries and vectors out of searches, recheck exact inputs before publication, discard changed-input builds, and replace an empty eligible set atomically
publish each regenerated summary with its vectors and pins atomically, keep independent successes, and block parents whose generated members remain stale
make summary status and both dry-runs read-only with no service calls, distinguish estimated build plans, and return complete regeneration/removal replies

serialize summary mutations with a nonblocking summary-operation lock, release pass locks during external calls, protect in-flight evidence by exact invocation liveness and clean up subprocesses/staging on interruption
hold for every directory of a repository's code corpus on disk one overview section that lists each of its code files

give for a file its classes, each with up to eight methods, and up to eight other named symbols, classes in the order of their names and methods and other symbols in the order of the file, with a count of what did not fit; and list a file without a named symbol by its name alone
make the overview from stored on-disk code file and chunk records alone, with no model and no network

reconcile the rendered outline as the last step of a pass, updating exactly the directory sections whose displayed text changed, including changes of symbol order, declaration kind, class membership and file path, and leave unchanged text and its embedding intact
keep the overview in the index store as chunks with the origin `overview`, and write no file for it
never mark an overview section stale, open no Drift for it, hold no edge from or to it, and delete it when its directory holds no code file any more
embed an overview section by the rules of MYC-3
let the overview sections of the searched repository compete in a search as documents do, leave them out of a search for code only, and return one with the origin `overview` and without a file
print on request the overview sections of a repository, or of one directory of it
not show a code result as documented in the overview
list every indexed code file, including empty files, in deterministic path/name/source-position order, and count all named declarations whether displayed or omitted
publish overview changes atomically from the code state the pass applied, delete empty directory sections and rebuild missing sections on a later pass without rereading unchanged files
have `overview` report only stored sections without a pass or writes, return an empty list normally for a valid absent directory, and refuse absolute or escaping `--dir` paths
start, for `mycel grep`, the first `grep` on the search path with exactly the arguments given, on its own standard input, output and error
end with grep's exit status, whatever happens to the tail
add nothing to grep's arguments and take nothing from them
find the pattern and the paths by grep's own rules for options: options with a value, a value written onto its option, short options written together, and `--`
print no tail when it meets an option it does not know
print the tail on standard output after grep's output, and leave it out in every case of the table above
